content: 1. Adjust the therapy or monitor the patient closely when administering dolutegravir. Administer dolutegravir (or abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine) at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking medications containing polyvalent cations. For dolutegravir/rilpivirine, administer at least 4 hours before or 6 hours after such medications. Polyvalent cations can interfere with dolutegravir absorption in the gastrointestinal tract, reducing its effectiveness. 2. Calcium carbonate and calcium citrate can decrease the levels or effects of dolutegravir by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer dolutegravir as described above to avoid this interaction. 3. Carbamazepine significantly reduces dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, there is insufficient data to recommend a dosage adjustment. 4. Dolutegravir increases the levels or effects of dalfampridine by inhibiting renal clearance. Monitor the patient closely for potential adverse effects. 5. Dolutegravir is contraindicated with dofetilide due to the risk of life-threatening arrhythmias caused by increased systemic exposure to dofetilide. This occurs because dolutegravir inhibits the renal organic cation transporter (OCT2), reducing dofetilide clearance. 6. Efavirenz decreases dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, increase the dolutegravir dose to 50 mg twice daily. 7. Elivaldogene autotemcel and dolutegravir may reduce each other’s effects. Avoid coadministration. Patients should discontinue antiretroviral therapy (ART) at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization medications and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 8. Etravirine significantly reduces dolutegravir plasma concentrations by inducing UGT1A and CYP3A enzymes. However, this effect is mitigated when etravirine is coadministered with lopinavir/ritonavir, darunavir/ritonavir, or atazanavir/ritonavir. Do not use etravirine with dolutegravir unless one of these protease inhibitors is also coadministered. 9. Ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate decrease dolutegravir levels by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer dolutegravir as described above to avoid this interaction. 10. Fosphenytoin and phenytoin reduce dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is insufficient data to recommend a dosage adjustment. 11. Magnesium-containing compounds (e.g., magnesium citrate, magnesium oxide, magnesium hydroxide) decrease dolutegravir levels by forming chelates in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer dolutegravir at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these compounds. 12. Multivitamins containing calcium, iron, or zinc can reduce dolutegravir levels by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer dolutegravir as described above to avoid this interaction. 13. Nevirapine reduces dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is insufficient data to recommend a dosage adjustment. 14. Orlistat may reduce dolutegravir levels by inhibiting its gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently in patients taking orlistat. If an increase in viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 15. Rifampin reduces dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Increase the dolutegravir dose when coadministering with strong UGT1A/CYP3A inducers like rifampin. Use an alternative to rifampin in patients with integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-associated resistance. 16. Selenium and zinc reduce dolutegravir levels by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer dolutegravir at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these supplements. 17. St. John’s Wort reduces dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is insufficient data to recommend a dosage adjustment. 18. Sucralfate decreases dolutegravir levels by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer dolutegravir as described above to avoid this interaction. 19. Tipranavir/ritonavir reduces dolutegravir levels by increasing its metabolism. Increase the dolutegravir dose to 50 mg twice daily when coadministering with strong UGT1A/CYP3A inducers like tipranavir/ritonavir. 20. Ublituximab may reduce dolutegravir’s effects due to its immunosuppressive properties, increasing the risk of infection. Monitor the patient closely. 21. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate decreases dolutegravir levels by inhibiting its gastrointestinal absorption. Administer dolutegravir at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these compounds. 22. Prussian blue reduces dolutegravir levels by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer dolutegravir as described above to avoid this interaction. 23. Dolutegravir is metabolized by UGT1A1 with some contribution from CYP3A. Its half-life is approximately 14 hours, and it is primarily excreted in feces (53% unchanged) and urine (31% as metabolites). Less than 1% is excreted unchanged in urine. 24. Dolutegravir is present in human milk, but its effects on milk production or breastfed infants are unknown. Breastfeeding carries potential risks, including HIV-1 transmission, development of viral resistance, and adverse reactions in the infant. 25. Dolutegravir is used with other HIV medications to control HIV infection. It reduces the amount of HIV in the body, improving immune function and lowering the risk of complications. It is not a cure for HIV. To prevent spreading HIV, continue taking all medications as prescribed and use effective barrier methods during sexual activity.
